checklist.note: The procedure code sends these claims to the named courts 'and no other'; whether that makes the rule one of public order is for the territorial-jurisdiction module, which has no final record.

checklist.item: Public prosecution is a principal party in family cases (Family Code article 3 bis); communication of the file to the prosecutor.

No limitation period for the tatliq action itself; but for harm-based grounds the time elapsed may matter as to proof; for maintenance arrears, the court may award maintenance from the date of the claim and, on proof, up to one year before it.
checklist.note: No text in the store sets a period for the tatliq action itself. The general limitations of the periods module concern obligations and are not imported.

checklist.item: Accessory request: maintenance of the wife during the waiting period (idda) and of the children, from the Family Code maintenance chapter.
Accessory request: custody of the children to the mother first, order of custodians, the child's interest; visitation right for the father.
Accessory request: housing for the custodian or rent allowance, charged to the father; the wife stays in the marital home until the judgment on housing is executed.
Accessory request: return of the wife's personal belongings, furniture and jewellery (household goods); rule on disputes about household goods (her word with oath for what is usual for women).
Accessory request: the deferred part of the dowry (sadaq), if unpaid.
checklist.note: Not among the usual request lines; the dowry statement is kept for the lawyer who adds it as a connected request.

checklist.item: Provisional measures: the judge may order urgent provisional measures by order on petition (maintenance, custody, visitation, housing) during the proceedings (Family Code article 57 bis).
Provisional execution: family judgments on maintenance, custody and housing are executory provisionally by law or at the judge's discretion.
checklist.note: The procedure code orders provisional execution on request for maintenance and the custodian's housing; in other cases only in urgency.

checklist.item: Documents: marriage certificate, family booklet, children's birth certificates, prior maintenance judgment and record of non-execution (bailiff), medical certificates, criminal judgment, proof of absence or abandonment, residence certificate.
Petition formal elements: identity of the parties, court, statement of facts and grounds, signed by the lawyer; fees.
checklist.note: Common to every claim; the petition-formal-elements module has no final record, so the procedure texts are cited directly (open point o11).

checklist.item: Boundary: khul (the wife's redemption by paying a sum, without proof of a ground) is a separate claim; divorce by the husband's will is a separate claim; divorce by mutual consent is a separate procedure.
Boundary: an action for maintenance only (without dissolution) or for return to the marital home is a distinct claim; tatliq for absence differs from a declaration of disappearance.
checklist.note: Return to the marital home is a separate family-section claim (court-sections.b7); no item of this record.

checklist.item: Boundary: polygamy without informing the wife gives her a right to tatliq and to ask the annulment of the new marriage if not consummated.

Foreign element: a defendant residing abroad (service abroad, longer periods for appearance); conflict of laws in the Civil Code for divorce (law of the husband's nationality at filing, Algerian law if one spouse is Algerian).
checklist.note: Service abroad itself is left to the shared modules.

checklist.item: Pending divorce or khul action between the same spouses: lis pendens or joinder.
Idda begins from the judgment; the wife's right to remarry and its link to the date of the judgment.
checklist.note: Waiting-period rules matter for the waiting-period maintenance requested; they set no period for filing.

checklist.item: Effect of the 2005 amendment: added grounds (breach of contract clauses, harm) and article 53 bis on compensation; the old version required less; check the version in force.
checklist.note: The store holds only the current wording of the grounds article and of the compensation article (ordinance 05-02); the 1984 wording is not in it. Searched the family-code text view for older wordings of articles 53 and 53 bis. Requested.

checklist.item: Is there a valid marriage between the parties, and is it registered or proved by a judgment of proof of marriage?
Is the plaintiff the wife, and is the defendant her husband (no divorce already pronounced between them)?
checklist.note: Capacity: a plaintiff lacking full capacity files through her guardian or curator (CPCA article 437); boundary n12 warns and open point o13 records the reading on a minor wife.

checklist.item: Which legal ground of taṭlīq is relied on: failure to maintain, defect, abandonment beyond four months, imprisonment, absence, serious harm, or another ground in the family code?
checklist.note: The ground is read through the proposed slots tatliq_ground_nonmaintenance, bed_desertion_ground and absence_ground (one per ground that has a checkable condition).

checklist.item: For failure to maintain: was there a prior judgment for maintenance, and did the husband stay in default after it? Is the wife aware of his means?
For abandonment: has the husband left the marital bed for more than four months, and how is it proved?
For harm (darar): what harm is legally recognised, and how is it proved (witnesses, medical certificate, criminal judgment)?
Which court has territorial jurisdiction in family matters (the place of the marital home, the custodian's residence, etc.) and is the rule of public order?
checklist.note: Public-order character not settled in the store's texts beyond 'and no other'.

checklist.item: Is the case listed before the family affairs section, and what if the court has no sections?
checklist.note: Answered by the record's own section rule (family; civil where the court has not created the section).

checklist.item: Is there a pending divorce, taṭlīq or khul action between the spouses (lis pendens)?
Is the conciliation attempt by the judge mandatory, within what period, and what is recorded in the minutes?
Must the public prosecutor be joined as a party in family cases?
What mandatory elements must the petition contain (names, addresses, facts, requests, grounds)?
Is there any limitation or forfeiture period for the taṭlīq claim, or is it open at any time?
checklist.note: No period for the tatliq claim itself; the three months of reconciliation are the judge's period after filing.

checklist.item: Is a formal notice required before filing (for maintenance or abandonment)?
checklist.note: No text in the store requires a notice before tatliq or before a maintenance or custody request; whether the Civil Code notice rule reaches compensation on tatliq is open point o7. The formal-notice module is not imported.

checklist.item: What documents must be attached: marriage certificate, family record, proof of the ground relied on, judgments, medical reports?
Which accessory requests can be joined: damages, maintenance of the wife during the waiting period, custody, children's maintenance, housing, personal belongings and jewellery?
What is the legal basis for damages in taṭlīq, and when are they granted?
How is the custody request governed: the custodian's rights, housing for the custodian, visitation?
Are the dowry and its unpaid balance claimable in the same action?
checklist.note: No text joins an unpaid dowry balance to the tatliq claim in terms; connected additional requests are allowed.

checklist.item: Is the judgment of taṭlīq open to appeal, and which parts are not?
Is provisional execution available for maintenance and housing parts?
Does the court appoint a judicial expert or hold an investigation (witness hearing) for the grounds?
What if the wife is abroad or the husband is abroad, or his address is unknown?
checklist.note: Defendant abroad: the longer period between service and first hearing; unknown address: the petition gives the last known domicile.

checklist.item: Is the claim of the wife in the waiting period (idda) maintenance part of the same petition?
What are the exits from the ordinary court: none expected, unless public bodies or criminal facts interfere?
checklist.note: Family claims stay with the family section; the only exit is the criminal one.

checklist.item: Is a criminal complaint on the same facts a bar to or a pause of the civil action?
Does the judge verify that the grounds are established before pronouncing the divorce, and how is the burden of proof placed?
Do the fees and legal aid rules apply to this claim?
checklist.note: Fees: applies, unless the law provides otherwise. Legal aid: ordinance 71-57 article 28 as replaced by law 09-02 (Official Journal 2009 no. 15, p. 11) grants it as of right to the plaintiff in a maintenance matter and to the mother in a custody matter; not yet in the store (open point o10, grade D; requested).

checklist.item: Does the person need to be represented by a lawyer before the family section?
checklist.note: A lawyer is compulsory only before appeal courts and the court of cassation.

checklist.item: Is the claim of restitution of the wife's furniture and jewellery proved by writing or by other means?

Store note on the Family Code articles cited: the text is certified as the current snapshot only and not for an earlier case; from which date does each wording apply, and what does it change for this unit?
checklist.note: The record cites the ordinance 05-02 wording of articles 3 bis, 7, 8, 8 bis, 8 bis 1, 19, 22, 37, 48, 49, 52, 53, 53 bis, 54, 57, 57 bis, 64 and 72 (Official Journal 2005 no. 15, 27 February 2005) and the law 84-11 wording of the others. The note says commencement follows Civil Code article 4 (one full day after publication in Algiers, after receipt elsewhere) with no single national date; Civil Code article 2 (not verified) applies a law only to the future. For a petition filed now the current wording applies to facts after March 2005; for older facts the earlier wording is not in the store (open point o6, grade D).

checklist.item: Store note on Civil Code article 12: amendment certification and commencement unresolved for the 2005 wording; temporal applicability unsettled. What does it change for this unit?
checklist.note: The text is not verified (grade D). The cited paragraph puts dissolution under the husband's national law at filing; the boundary only warns and asks the lawyer to check.

checklist.item: Store note on Civil Code article 13: original 1975 text; the Arabic cross-reference (articles 11 and 12) differs from the French print (12 and 13), and temporal applicability is unsettled. Does it still govern divorce with a foreign element?
checklist.note: Cited in the Arabic wording, which refers to the articles on validity of marriage and on its effects and dissolution; not verified (grade D); the boundary only warns.

checklist.item: Penal Code: which offences touch the family's honour (conviction ground), abandonment of the family; Code of Criminal Procedure on deferring the civil case.
checklist.note: Searched the store's codes (cpca, civil-code, family-code, commercial-code, labour texts, law-22-13): no Penal Code or Code of Criminal Procedure. Requested. The verifier read Penal Code article 330 item 2 (abandonment of the wife for more than two months) in the Official Journal, 2015 no. 71, p. 4; recorded in open point o5 and requested.

checklist.item: Neighbour flag: cpca 40 ¶10 (work-accident exception to the labour territorial rule).
checklist.note: The paragraph is an exception to the labour-dispute item of the article; it says nothing on family claims, whose item (¶3) is cited by b42.

checklist.item: Neighbour flag: cpca 21 ¶2 (the judge may accept ordinary copies of documents).
checklist.note: It relaxes the general rule on lodging documents in every claim; it changes nothing in the documents listed for tatliq (open point o11).

checklist.item: Neighbour flag: cpca 22 ¶1 (documents handed to the registrar for inventory before they enter the file, on pain of rejection).
checklist.note: A general rule on lodging documents in every claim, for the petition-formal-elements module; it adds no document particular to tatliq (open point o11).

Unregistered marriage.

Attack adv-1: a wife of 18, married with the judge's leave, files in her own name: the capacity boundary warns.
Attack adv-2: the mother asks tatliq, maintenance and custody: the fee document now names the legal-aid decision and is still listed.

Attack adv-3: persistent discord, no harm proved: the discord ground's element (e5) now cites the procedure code's arbitrator rules with both readings (o14); nothing is asked or warned, the proof document is listed.

Attack adv-6: desertion for over four months and a criminal complaint for abandonment of the wife: the desertion boundary is silent and the proof document is listed (the imported criminal exit x6, which the examples tool does not run, warns in the final record).
Attack adv-7: the couple's last marital home was in France and the wife files in Algeria: the marital-home boundary warns.
Attack adv-8: marriage certificate drawn up abroad in French: the marriage document is listed with its official-translation condition.
